title: Generalized Triangular Reciprocals via Harmonic Numbers
description: For every k ≥ 1, ∑_{n=1}^∞ 1/(n(n+k)) = H_k/k, where H_k is the k-th harmonic number. Generalizes the classical Leibniz identity (k=1 case).

overview.historicalContext: The k=1 case ∑_{n=1}^∞ 1/(n(n+1)) = 1 (or its scaled form ∑ 2/(n(n+1)) = 2) was given by Leibniz in 1673 via telescoping, and appears as Wiedijk problem 42. The general identity ∑_{n=1}^∞ 1/(n(n+k)) = H_k/k is recorded in Gradshteyn & Ryzhik §0.234.2 and connects directly to the digamma function via Abramowitz & Stegun §6.3.5: ψ(x+1) = -γ + ∑_{n=1}^∞ x/(n(n+x)). The harmonic numbers H_k themselves go back to Pythagoras and were systematically studied by Mengoli (1647) and the Bernoullis. Mathlib's `harmonic` definition (rational-valued) and David Loeffler's 2024 `deriv_Gamma_nat` lemma make the formalization tractable: the partial-fraction telescoping yields a finite difference of harmonic numbers that converges to zero, and the closed form drops out.
overview.problemStatement:
**Generalized Triangular Reciprocals**: For every integer $k \ge 1$,

$$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n(n+k)} = \frac{H_k}{k},$$

where $H_k = \sum_{i=1}^{k} \frac{1}{i}$ is the $k$-th harmonic number.
overview.text: Generalizes Leibniz's ∑1/(n(n+1)) = 1 to arbitrary shift k. The sum equals (H_1 + H_2 + ... + H_k)/(k·…) -- more precisely, H_k/k, the average of the first k reciprocals.
overview.proofStrategy: 1. Partial-fraction decomposition 1/(n(n+k)) = (1/k)(1/n - 1/(n+k)). 2. Split the partial sum ∑_{n=1}^N into two harmonic-like pieces; reindex the shifted sum via Finset.sum_Ico_add' (c := k). The harmonic differences are read off via harmonic_eq_sum_Icc + Finset.sum_Ico_consecutive, yielding S_N(k) = (1/k)(H_k - (H_{N+k} - H_N)). 3. Show H_{N+k} - H_N → 0 by induction on k (succ step uses tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat composed with the shift). 4. Conclude via hasSum_iff_tendsto_nat_of_nonneg: partial sums tend to H_k/k.
keyInsights: Partial fractions reduce the product 1/(n(n+k)) to a telescoping-like difference, but with a gap of size k rather than 1 — the cancellation no longer happens within consecutive terms but across a sliding window
The tail H_{N+k} - H_N is bounded above by k/(N+1) since each of its k terms is at most 1/(N+1), so the tail vanishes for any fixed k; the proof structures this as an induction on k

Mathlib's `harmonic : ℕ → ℚ` lives in ℚ but the series is real; the cast site is at the statement level (harmonic k : ℝ), with push_cast bridging inside lemmas — this matches the sibling `triangular-reciprocals-oq-03` convention
Reindexing via `Finset.sum_Ico_add'` is the same lemma harmonic_eq_sum_Icc uses internally, so the harmonic differences fall out without manual index gymnastics

The Aristotle companion file exposes only the supporting lemmas (partial_fraction, tail_to_zero, summability) — not the main HasSum — keeping the open-question identity out of the automated proof-search loop

sections.title: Lemma 1: Partial Fraction Decomposition
sections.summary: Establishes 1/(n(n+k)) = (1/k)(1/n - 1/(n+k)) for n,k ≠ 0, transferred verbatim from the alternating sibling's proof. Closed by `field_simp; ring`.
sections.mathContext: Algebraic identity: $\frac{1}{n(n+k)} = \frac{1}{k}\left(\frac{1}{n} - \frac{1}{n+k}\right)$. The factor $1/k$ is what scales the harmonic sum on the right of the main identity.

sections.title: Lemma 2: Partial Sum Closed Form
sections.summary: Computes ∑_{n=1}^N 1/(n(n+k)) = (1/k)(H_k - (H_{N+k} - H_N)). Applies partial_fraction termwise, splits via Finset.sum_sub_distrib, reindexes the second sum by m = n+k using Finset.sum_Ico_add', and identifies harmonic differences via harmonic_eq_sum_Icc + Finset.sum_Ico_consecutive.
sections.mathContext: Closed form for the partial sum: $S_N(k) = \frac{1}{k}\bigl(H_k - (H_{N+k} - H_N)\bigr)$. The telescoping gap of size $k$ leaves an $H_k$-sized residue when the window slides off the start, plus a vanishing tail $H_{N+k} - H_N$.

sections.title: Lemma 3: Tail Decay
sections.summary: Shows H_{N+k} - H_N → 0 as N → ∞ for fixed k, by induction on k. Succ step uses tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat composed with the shift, plus harmonic_succ. Required care to avoid ContinuousSMul ℚ≥0 typeclass instability — bind RHS to typed `have` first.
sections.mathContext: Tail estimate: $0 \le H_{N+k} - H_N \le k/(N+1) \to 0$. Each of the $k$ terms in the difference is at most $1/(N+1)$, and the sum of $k$ copies of a vanishing sequence still vanishes.

sections.title: Lemma 4: Summability
sections.summary: Establishes Summable (fun n => 1/((n+1)·((n+1)+k))) by comparison with 1/(n+1)^2 (p-series at p=2). Uses Summable.of_nonneg_of_le and summable_nat_add_iff to shift index by 1.

sections.title: Main Theorem: HasSum H_k/k
sections.summary: Main result: HasSum (fun n => 1/((n+1)((n+1)+k))) (H_k/k). Uses hasSum_iff_tendsto_nat_of_nonneg, identifies the range-N partial sum with the Icc 1 N form via Finset.sum_Ico_add', applies Lemma 2's closed form, and takes the limit using Lemma 3's tail decay through (tendsto_const_nhds.sub h_tail).const_mul (1/k). Includes the tsum corollary.
sections.mathContext: Main identity: $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n(n+k)} = \frac{H_k}{k}$. As $N \to \infty$, the closed form $(1/k)(H_k - (H_{N+k} - H_N))$ approaches $(1/k)(H_k - 0) = H_k/k$.

sections.title: Special Cases k = 1, 2, 3
sections.summary: Verifies H_1/1 = 1 (classical Leibniz), H_2/2 = 3/4, H_3/3 = 11/18 by unfolding `harmonic_succ` repeatedly and closing with `push_cast; norm_num`.
sections.mathContext: Sanity checks: $H_1/1 = 1$, $H_2/2 = (1 + 1/2)/2 = 3/4$, $H_3/3 = (1 + 1/2 + 1/3)/3 = 11/18$. The k=1 case is exactly Leibniz's identity, confirming the generalization recovers the base case.

crossReferences.description: Generalizes the classical Leibniz identity ∑2/(n(n+1)) = 2 (Wiedijk 42, k=1 scaled case) to arbitrary k ≥ 1, recovering H_k/k. The k=1 special case explicitly recovers H_1/1 = 1.

Sibling alternating analogue ∑(-1)^{n+1}·2/(n(n+1)) = 4·ln(2) - 2. Both use the same `partial_fraction` lemma; this proof lifts the lemma verbatim. The alternating case requires Abel's theorem (axiomatized); the non-alternating general case proved here is fully verified.
Sibling figurate-number reciprocal sums (in-progress). Both generalize triangular-reciprocals in different directions — this proof varies the shift k while oq-01 varies the figurate dimension.

Uses Mathlib's `harmonic : ℕ → ℚ` definition and `harmonic_eq_sum_Icc`, which underlie the divergence proofs in the harmonic-divergence family. This proof's tail decay H_{N+k} - H_N → 0 is the convergent counterpart to harmonic divergence.
Summability of 1/(n(n+k)) is established by comparison with ∑1/n² (Basel). Both express rational-coefficient series with closed forms — Basel gets π²/6, this gets H_k/k.

conclusion.summary: The generalized identity ∑_{n=1}^∞ 1/(n(n+k)) = H_k/k is fully verified in Lean 4 (Mathlib v4.26.0) with 0 sorries and 0 axioms. The proof closes the open question OQ-02 of the triangular-reciprocals series and demonstrates that the partial-fraction + harmonic-telescoping technique scales cleanly from k=1 (Leibniz) to arbitrary k.
conclusion.implications: This result provides the analytic backbone for several follow-ups: (1) digamma reformulation (H_k/k = (ψ(k+1) + γ)/k) via `Real.deriv_Gamma_nat`, (2) extension to non-integer k via the digamma series, and (3) connection to the alternating sibling's transcendental closed forms. Recovers Leibniz as the k=1 case and exposes the harmonic numbers as the natural one-parameter family.
